extraction.name: FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation
extraction.description: FLORES-101 is an evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages. It covers a variety of topics and domains, enabling assessment of model quality on low-resource languages and many-to-many multilingual translation.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.citeAs: Goyal, N., Gao, C., Chaudhary, V., Chen, P.-J., Wenzek, G., Ju, D., Krishnan, S., Ranzato, M., Guzmán, F., & Fan, A. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2106.03193.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were sourced from English Wikipedia (including Wikinews, Wikijunior, and Wikivoyage) and professionally translated into 101 languages through a controlled process involving multiple Language Service Providers (LSPs), automatic checks, and human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia (including Wikinews, Wikijunior, and Wikivoyage)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentence selection: articles randomly selected from each source, then 3-5 contiguous sentences manually selected, avoiding very short or malformed sentences. Paragraphs balanced by location (beginning, middle, end). Sentences labeled by sub-topic (10 categories).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Professional translators translated sentences. Quality assurance (QA) performed by independent LSPs. Translations automatically checked for language identification, copy detection, length, fluency, and similarity to commercial engines. Human evaluation using Translation Quality Score (0-100) based on error categories (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, register). Acceptable threshold: 90%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Mistranslation was the largest error category. Error variation by domain within a language, but no clear trend across languages. All domains challenging for human translators.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 10 annotators for sentence selection: 6 male, 4 female; roles: researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SentencePiece tokenizer for spBLEU metric; sacrebleu for BLEU computation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Test set not released publicly but available via evaluation server to prevent overfitting. Dev and devtest splits publicly downloadable. Dataset intended for use in evaluation campaigns like WMT 2021 Large-Scale Multilingual Task.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in low-resource machine translation, benefiting speakers of low-resource languages who currently lack good translation support.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Source sentences from English Wikipedia may introduce cultural or topical biases. Translationese effects may be present but considered marginal for low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Translations may exhibit translationese (overly literal or awkward translations). Some languages were excluded after failing to meet quality threshold. Many-to-many evaluation requires source sentences not in English to be produced by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of machine translation models (especially low-resource and multilingual), document-level translation, multimodal translation, sentence and document classification, language identification, multilingual domain adaptation.
